item.text:
`Plant` now participates in the same capability model as animals instead of sitting off to the side. I generalized [`Ageable.java`](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R008_module_java/Ageable.java:1) so it models lifecycle progression rather than only age-based death, and generalized [`Breedable.java`](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R008_module_java/Breedable.java:1) so it no longer assumes animal-specific disease inheritance or `Animal.class` breeding space rules.

With that in place, [`Plant.java`](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R008_module_java/Plant.java:9) now implements `Ageable` and `Breedable`. Its growth is handled through `applyAgeProgression()`, and its spreading goes through the shared `populateOffspring(...)` pattern with plant-specific hooks for breeding space and offspring count. On the animal side, [`Animal.java`](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R008_module_java/Animal.java:7) was updated to match the more general interfaces, so both plants and animals now use the same capability contracts for lifecycle and reproduction while keeping their domain-specific rules.

The result is a more consistent hierarchy: shared patterns live in the capability interfaces, while species-specific policies stay in the concrete classes. `Plant` still keeps its own health/spread behavior, but it now plugs into the same modular structure as the animal classes.
